I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. It imports `words` and `groupBy` from `es-toolkit` and `truncate` from `es-toolkit/compat`. I couldn't compare it against the original lodash version because lodash isn't installed here, and I didn't install it. `src/module.ts` fails type checking and bundling for the same reason.

| Function | Source | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `words` | `es-toolkit` | It matched compat `words` on 200,000 random strings built from letters, digits, spaces, hyphens, underscores and periods. |
| `groupBy` | `es-toolkit` | The strict version takes a function, so `'age'` became `r => r.age`. The keys are still strings, as before. |
| `truncate` | `es-toolkit/compat` | The strict package has no `truncate`. The `{ length: 24 }` call is unchanged and I spot-checked that it truncates with `...`. |

The signatures and the `Row` and `Config` exports are unchanged, and I wrote no replacement code of my own. The only change to your code is the `groupBy` key function.

`npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 807 bytes (min+gzip), with 99 bytes of my own code in the bundle. Moving `words` and `groupBy` to compat as well came to 4288 bytes, so the strict versions are much smaller.

`tsc` reports no errors for `out/module.ts`. I didn't diff the results against lodash itself, so the first check, that results equal the original, is untested.

I didn't write a before/after table or doc links for the three functions.
